title: Theoretical ab initio Evolution of Satellite Intensity near Threshold for Cu K-shell transitions
authors: Daniel Pinheiro, Gonçalo Baptista, César Godinho, André Fernandes, Jorge Machado, Pedro Amaro, Nancy Paul, Martino Trassinelli, Miguel Avillez, Paul Indelicato, José Paulo Santos, Mauro Guerra
abstract: In this work, we have investigated the evolution of satellite intensity near the ionization threshold for Cu K-shell transitions through theoretical methods. Employing standard state-of-the-art ab initio methods, we have calculated all Cu K-shell transitions and simulated the full K$α_1$ and K$α_2$ spectrum where all transition parameters, as well as shake probabilities were determined theoretically. Through these calculations we show that standard state-of-the-art ab initio methods achieve good agreement with experiment and enable us to simulate the intensity evolution near ionization thresholds within a good margin of error. Below-threshold satellite intensity was found to originate from resonant 1s$\rightarrow$3d and 1s$\rightarrow$4p excitations in Cu(I) and Cu(II) oxide phases respectively, which were included in our simulations.
summary: This paper theoretically models the evolution of satellite X-ray emission intensity near ionization thresholds for Copper K-shell transitions. Using sophisticated ab initio calculations, the authors demonstrate that their methods accurately predict spectral changes by accounting for shake processes originating from specific resonant excitations in oxide compounds. This provides a powerful tool for high-resolution spectroscopy.
main_problem: The study investigates how satellite X-ray emission intensity evolves near the ionization threshold for Cu K-shell transitions.
main_result: Standard ab initio methods successfully simulate this intensity evolution with good agreement to experiment, identifying below-threshold satellites originating from specific resonant excitations in oxide phases.
method: The research employs state-of-the-art ab initio theoretical calculations using the Multiconfiguration Dirac-Fock code (MCDFGME) to model radiative and non-radiative decay processes.
model_or_system: The system under study is Copper (Cu) atoms/ions, specifically examining K-shell transitions in $	ext{Cu(I)}$ and $	ext{Cu(II)}$ oxide phases. The theoretical framework models the transition intensity by incorporating shake probabilities derived from atomic structure calculations.
key_observables: Satellite intensity ($K\alpha_1$ and $K\alpha_2$), total decay width ($\Gamma_i$), shake probabilities (shake-off and shake-up), and spectral line shape modulation near thresholds.
important_parameters: Ionization threshold energy, excitation energies, binding energies, and the relative contributions of different excitation channels ($1s	o 3d$, $1s	o 4p$).
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the Sudden Approximation (SA) for shake processes; solid-state effects are noted as a potential source of discrepancy with experiment.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the overlap integral between beam Gaussian profiles and initial level Lorentzian profiles, and show simulated synthetic spectra for Cu K$\alpha_{1,2}$ including all satellite contributions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by detailing theoretical models (Thomas/Roy), implementing calculations using MCDFGME to determine transition rates and shake probabilities, modeling the energy dependence via overlap integrals, and finally comparing these simulations against experimental observations for Cu oxide species.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it applies advanced quantum mechanical methods to model complex many-body dynamics (shake processes) in atomic/solid-state spectra, which shares mathematical techniques with open quantum systems modeling.
